# 2 Samuel Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 168v–169r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_001_page_001.jpg, 2SA_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1:1** And-it-was after [the]-death of-Sha'ul, and-David had-returned from-striking the-Amaleqi, and-David sat in-Tsiqlag two days.

**1:2** And-it-was on-the-day the-third, and-behold, a-man came from the-camp, from-with Sha'ul, and-his-garments [were]-torn, and-earth [was] upon his-head. And-it-was when-he-came to David, and-he-fell to-the-ground and-bowed-down.

**1:3** And-said to-him David, "From-where do-you-come?" And-he-said to-him, "From-[the]-camp of-Yisra'el I-escaped."

**1:4** And-said to-him David, "What was the-word? Tell me, please." And-he-said, "That the-people fled from the-battle, and-also many from the-people fell and-died, and-also Sha'ul and-Yehonatan his-son died."

**1:5** And-said David to the-youth who-told him, "How do-you-know that Sha'ul died and-Yehonatan his-son?"

**1:6** And-said the-youth who-told him, "Happening I-happened [i.e., by chance I came] upon-mount the-Gilboa, and-behold Sha'ul [was]-leaning upon his-spear, and-behold the-chariots and-the-masters of-the-horsemen pressed-upon-him.

**1:7** And-he-turned behind-him and-saw-me, and-called to-me, and-I-said, 'Behold-me' [hinneni].

**1:8** And-he-said to-me, 'Who [are]-you?' And-I-said to-him, 'An-Amaleqi [am]-I.'

**1:9** And-he-said to-me, 'Stand, please, upon-me and-kill-me, for seized-me the-anguish [shavats], for all still my-life [is]-in-me.'

**1:10** And-I-stood upon-him and-killed-him, for I-knew that not he-would-live after his-falling. And-I-took the-crown that [was] upon-his-head and-the-bracelet that [was] upon-his-arm, and-I-brought-them to-my-lord here."

**1:11** And-seized David his-garments and-tore-them, and-also all the-men who [were] with-him.

**1:12** And-they-mourned and-wept and-fasted until the-evening for-Sha'ul and-for-Yehonatan his-son and-for-[the]-people of-YHWH and-for-[the]-house of-Yisra'el, for they-fell by-the-sword.

**1:13** And-said David to the-youth who-told him, "From-where [are]-you?" And-he-said, "Son of-a-man sojourner, an-Amaleqi [am]-I."

**1:14** And-said to-him David, "How were-you-not afraid to-stretch-out your-hand to-destroy [the]-anointed-one [meshiach] of-YHWH?"

**1:15** And-called David to-one of-the-youths and-said, "Draw-near, strike-him." And-he-struck-him, and-he-died.

**1:16** And-said to-him David, "Your-blood [is] upon-your-head, for your-mouth testified against-you, saying, 'I killed [the]-anointed-one [meshiach] of-YHWH.'"

**1:17** And-lamented David this lamentation [qinah] over Sha'ul and-over Yehonatan his-son.

**1:18** And-he-said to-teach [the]-sons of-Yehudah "The-Bow" [Qeshet]. Behold, [it is]-written upon [the]-Book of-the-Upright [Sefer ha-Yashar]:

**1:19** "The-beauty [tsevi], O-Yisra'el, upon-your-heights [is]-slain!
How have-fallen [the]-mighty-ones [gibborim]!

**1:20** Do-not tell [it] in-Gat,
do-not proclaim [it] in-[the]-streets of-Ashqelon,
lest rejoice [the]-daughters of-[the]-Pelishtim,
lest exult [the]-daughters of-the-uncircumcised.

**1:21** Mountains of-the-Gilboa,
no dew and-no rain upon-you, and-[no]-fields of-offerings [terumot]!
For there was-defiled [the]-shield of-[the]-mighty-ones [gibborim],
[the]-shield of-Sha'ul — not anointed with-oil.

**1:22** From-[the]-blood of-[the]-slain,
from-[the]-fat of-[the]-mighty-ones [gibborim],
[the]-bow of-Yehonatan did-not turn-back,
and-[the]-sword of-Sha'ul did-not return empty.

**1:23** Sha'ul and-Yehonatan,
the-beloved and-the-pleasant in-their-lives,
and-in-their-death they-were-not divided.
From-eagles they-were-swifter,
from-lions they-were-stronger.

**1:24** Daughters of-Yisra'el, to Sha'ul weep,
who-clothed-you [in]-scarlet with-luxuries,
who-placed ornaments of-gold upon-your-garments.

**1:25** How have-fallen [the]-mighty-ones [gibborim] in-[the]-midst of-the-battle!
Yehonatan, upon-your-heights [is]-slain!

**1:26** I-am-distressed for-you, my-brother Yehonatan.
You-were-very pleasant to-me.
Wonderful [was]-your-love to-me,
surpassing [the]-love of-women.

**1:27** How have-fallen [the]-mighty-ones [gibborim],
and-perished [the]-weapons of-war!"

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.6 — niqroh niqreti:** Infinitive absolute construction (*happening I happened*) emphasizing the chance nature of the encounter. The narrator uses this to foreground the Amalekite's self-serving account.

**v.9 — shavats:** A rare word (hapax legomenon in the verbal form here) denoting a cramping agony or convulsion. Some scholars connect it to the writhing of death throes. I preserve it as "anguish" but note its unique character.

**v.18 — Qeshet:** The word "Bow" (קֶשֶׁת) appears to be the title of the lament. The Masoretic text reads *lelammed bney-yehudah qeshet* — "to teach the sons of Judah 'The Bow.'" Some scholars emend or reinterpret, but the LC text is clear.

**v.19 — ha-tsevi:** The word צְבִי can mean "gazelle," "beauty," "glory," or "honor." I render "the beauty" following the primary sense of adornment/splendor, but the animal imagery (gazelle slain on the heights) may be intentional double-meaning.

**v.21 — sedey terumot:** An extremely difficult phrase. The MT reads שְׂדֵי תְרוּמֹת, "fields of offerings" or "fields of uplifted-things." Some emend to "fields of first-fruits" or "upsurging fields." The curse invokes agricultural barrenness on the mountains where the mighty fell.

**v.26 — ahavatkha li:** David's grief for Jonathan uses the noun אַהֲבָה (*love*), the same word used for covenantal, familial, and romantic love throughout the Hebrew Bible. The text draws no distinction; the word carries the full weight of the covenant-bond between them.

**4QSamᵃ note:** The Dead Sea Scrolls fragments (4Q51) preserve portions of 2 Samuel with significant textual variants. For chapter 1, the major witnesses remain the MT (Leningrad Codex) and the LXX (Vaticanus/Sinaiticus as "2 Kingdoms"). Translators should note that the LXX occasionally preserves a shorter text.

*— EMET*
